newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-COACH PAYS TRIBUTE TO AKII-BUA..
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-COACH PAYS TRIBUTE TO AKII-BUA..

text.p: Malcolm Arnold, who coached John Akii-Bua to the 400 metres hurdles gold medal at the 1972 Munich Olympics, on Sunday paid tribute to the Ugandan athlete who died on Friday.
"It is a terrible irony. I was only talking to people yesterday about the Olympics here and John winning," the British coach, in Munich for the European Cup, said.
"As an athlete he was very much like Colin Jackson (110 metres hurdles world record holder whom Arnold also coaches). They both had the same characteristics.
"John always worked very hard and he got what he deserved as far as athletic achievement was concerned."
Arnold was Ugandan head coach between 1968 and 1972.

He was in Munich this weekend for the first time since the 1972 Olympics in his present role as the British Athletic Federation head coach. Britain's men won the European Cup for the first time since Arnold took over the position in 1994.
Arnold had lost contact with Akii-Bua in recent years.
"Sadly I didn't know he was ill, although occasionally I used to hear about what he was doing from Ugandan coaches I used to meet at international competitions."
Despite the fact that the pair had not spoken for several years, Akii-Bua was still not far from Arnold's thoughts.

On Saturday, not knowing of Akii-Bua's grave condition, he watched the European Cup from the seat in the Olympic Stadium in which he had sat to watch Akii-Bua win Uganda's first and, to date, only Olympic gold medal.
